text: Why is the Internet's protocol architecture drawn as an hourglass?
choices: Because traffic flows in both directions
Many applications above and many link technologies below, with exactly one protocol at the waist
Because it was designed in the 1970s
To show the passage of time
explanation: 'Everything over IP, and IP over everything.' A new link technology needs only to carry IP; a new application needs only to run over IP. Neither has to ask permission — and this is also why IPv6 has taken thirty years, because the waist is the hardest thing to change.
